jurisdiction.name: Philippines
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: The Philippines has no AI-specific law. AI governance runs through the trade department's national AI roadmaps (2021 and 2024), the Data Privacy Act of 2012 with the privacy commission's December 2024 advisory on applying it to AI systems, a joint circular on AI in government (draft 2024, reported final 2026), the education department's 2026 AI guidelines for basic education, and the central bank's 2026 AI governance principles for financial institutions. Many AI and deepfake bills are pending in Congress.
lead_institutions: Department of Information and Communications Technology
narrative.review_notes: Rechecked on 18 October 2026: the privacy commission, civil service commission, trade department and House document sites opened, so the Data Privacy Act and the privacy commission's AI advisory were read in full. The Official Gazette, the ICT and education departments, the securities regulator, the development planning department and both chambers' main websites still could not be accessed, so the 2026 joint circular on AI in government and the education department's AI order remain unconfirmed.

instruments.official_title: Memorandum No. M-2026-031: Guidance Paper Entitled “Governance Principles for Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Financial Services”
instruments.english_title: BSP Memorandum No. M-2026-031: Governance Principles for Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Financial Services
instruments.issuing_authority: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (Office of the Deputy Governor, Financial Supervision Sector)
instruments.current_status: Signed by Deputy Governor Lyn I. Javier on 24 June 2026 and addressed to all BSP-supervised financial institutions. The guidance states it is non-binding and voluntary but sets minimum supervisory expectations; it notes a forthcoming BSP Model Risk Management framework for algorithmic fairness and model risk.
instruments.summary: BSP memorandum issuing a guidance paper that asks BSP-supervised financial institutions to formally develop their own AI governance framework, proportionate to the materiality and complexity of their AI systems. It sets out the 'STARS' principles (sustainability, transparency, accountability, responsibility, security), maps risks and mitigating controls across the AI system lifecycle, and extends to outsourced service providers under a shared-responsibility model. The principles are stated to be non-binding and voluntary, but described as minimum supervisory expectations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main AI-specific guidance from the Philippine financial supervisor.

instruments.official_title: Republic Act No. 10173: An Act Protecting Individual Personal Information in Information and Communications Systems in the Government and the Private Sector, Creating for this Purpose a National Privacy Commission, and for Other Purposes (Data Privacy Act of 2012)
instruments.english_title: Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173)
instruments.current_status: Approved by the President on 15 August 2012 and in force. The Act states that it takes effect fifteen days after publication in at least two national newspapers of general circulation. The privacy commission applies it to AI systems through NPC Advisory No. 2024-04.
instruments.summary: The Philippines' general data protection law, governing processing of personal information by government and private-sector controllers and processors and creating the National Privacy Commission. It governs the collection and use of personal data for training and operating AI systems, and is the legal basis for the NPC's 2024 AI advisory.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data-protection law that governs AI processing of personal data.

instruments.official_title: DepEd Order No. 003, s. 2026: Foundational Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Basic Education
instruments.english_title: DepEd Order No. 3, s. 2026: Foundational Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Basic Education
instruments.current_status: Listed on the DepEd issuances page with the date 20 February 2026. Content details come from DepEd's own 26 February 2026 news item and need confirmation against the order.
instruments.summary: Department order setting national foundational guidelines for AI use by learners, teachers and offices in basic education. It reportedly introduces a risk-based classification with prohibited uses (e.g. emotion recognition, social scoring, manipulative chatbots aimed at minors), requires privacy impact assessments before deployment, and requires AI deployments to be recorded in a DepEd AI Registry.

instruments.official_title: NPC Advisory No. 2024-04: Guidelines on the Application of Republic Act No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA), its Implementing Rules and Regulations, and the Issuances of the Commission to Artificial Intelligence Systems Processing Personal Data
instruments.english_title: NPC Advisory No. 2024-04: Guidelines on applying the Data Privacy Act of 2012 to AI systems processing personal data
instruments.current_status: Advisory dated 19 December 2024, signed by the Privacy Commissioner and two Deputy Privacy Commissioners, and listed on the privacy commission's advisories page.
instruments.summary: Privacy commission advisory explaining how the Data Privacy Act, its implementing rules and the commission's issuances apply when personal data is processed in developing or deploying AI systems, including training and testing. It sets expectations on transparency (explaining purposes, inputs, risks, outputs and impacts of AI processing), accountability (documented measures, responsibility for outsourced processing), fairness, accuracy, data minimisation, lawful basis including for publicly available data, and mechanisms to uphold data subject rights.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main AI-specific guidance from the Philippine data protection authority.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The Philippines' official gazette, Congress, the trade, ICT and science departments, other departments and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for strategy, government AI governance, procurement, cybersecurity, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, international agreements or historical publications. Many official sites, including the Official Gazette, the privacy commission, the education agencies, the ICT department, the securities regulator, the Senate and the House, were unavailable, and the standards bureau and the health and labour departments are still to be checked in depth.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. privacy.gov.ph, officialgazette.gov.ph (and mirror), deped.gov.ph, ched.gov.ph, dict.gov.ph, ictstatistics.dict.gov.ph, csc.gov.ph, sec.gov.ph, senate.gov.ph and congress.gov.ph returned 403 to curl and WebFetch; ncc.gov.ph proxy 502. Bureau of Philippine Standards and DOLE not searched. NPC advisory and DepEd order summaries from the agencies' own indexed pages (located only). Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Official Gazette (blocked; RA 10173 located), House of Representatives document server (HB 11007 read), Senate (blocked; SB 25 via discovery). No enacted AI-specific law or deepfake statute found; deepfake bills pending.; Government: DTI (site reachable; only press releases on the 2021 roadmap and NAISR 2.0, no full text), DICT ICT Knowledge Portal (blocked; 2024 draft JMC and 2026 JMC 003 located), DOST site search (nothing AI-governance specific).; Ministries: DepEd (DO 003 s. 2026 located; site blocked), CHED (no issued AI order found; planned policy only), DOH searched, no AI administrative order found; DOST: NAIS-PH announced 2025 but no official text (lead).; Regulators: BSP (M-2026-031 read), NPC (Advisory 2024-04 located; site blocked), SEC (blocked; no AI issuance found in search), NTC/telecom: searched, nothing found.. Not reached: officialgazette.gov.ph, privacy.gov.ph, deped.gov.ph, ched.gov.ph, dict.gov.ph, csc.gov.ph, sec.gov.ph, senate.gov.ph, congress.gov.ph: all return HTTP 403 bot-protection challenges to curl and WebFetch; ncc.gov.ph / cybersecurity: proxy CONNECT 502; National standards body (Bureau of Philippine Standards): not reached in time box; Health (DOH) and labour (DOLE) AI documents: not searched in depth. Could not verify: All Cloudflare-protected PH government sites (privacy, gazette, deped, dict, csc, sec, ched, senate) blocked curl and WebFetch with HTTP 403. strategy, government-governance, procurement, cyber-security, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, international, historical: no material found. Local retry 2026-10-18 (home connection, Saudi Arabia, ~20 min): opened: privacy.gov.ph (advisories page and PDFs; DPA PDF via curl, AI advisory PDF via headless browser after curl connection reset; old 2024/12 advisory path now 404), csc.gov.ph (curl 200; no AI JMC in listings), dti.gov.ph search (200), docs.congress.hrep.online (HB 11007 PDF via headless browser). Still failing: officialgazette.gov.ph, dict.gov.ph (incl. /ictstatistics/ and /department-circulars), ictstatistics.dict.gov.ph, sec.gov.ph, congress.gov.ph, depdev.gov.ph: HTTP 403 bot-verification for curl and headless browser; deped.gov.ph 403/blank; web.senate.gov.ph Cloudflare 523 origin unreachable.
